How to read the Sheriff notes, and what each sale type means for a bidder

Educational, Pennsylvania / Allegheny County context — not legal advice. Title outcomes at a sheriff sale depend on lien priority and notice; have a PA title company or real-estate attorney confirm before bidding on any specific parcel.
Tax lien (Sci Fa sur tax lien)

A school district, municipality or the County is enforcing unpaid real-estate tax claims through a writ of scire facias. The Cost & Tax bid is the opening bid covering the claim plus costs. Which other liens are wiped out depends on priority and proper notice — do not assume "free and clear" unless there is a free & clear court order.
Free & clear court order (F/C O/C) + min bid
The court has authorized sale free and clear of liens at the stated minimum bid, which can be far below the listed Cost & Tax bid. Read the actual order on the docket to confirm scope.

A lender is selling under its foreclosure judgment. The Cost & Tax bid is only costs and taxes; the lender can credit-bid up to its judgment (see "Reassessed damages"), so outside bidders usually need to beat the lender's announced bid. Liens senior to the mortgage can survive.

An association is executing on a money judgment for unpaid assessments (AR- case numbers). Because this is usually a junior lien, a first mortgage on the unit may survive the sale — potentially a large hidden liability. Get a title search before bidding.
A creditor executing on a general money judgment (e.g., business lenders). Senior liens and mortgages typically survive.
A municipal claim (non-tax, e.g., sewer/water/demolition) enforced by sheriff sale.
Scheduled to go to the upcoming sale — but the Sheriff will only sell if the paperwork is complete (see the four boxes and notes).
Moved to the date shown. 12/31/2099 = indefinite (Save Your Home program). The meaning of "(Waived)" is not stated on the list.
Sale halted (bankruptcy, payment plan, court order). "Amount realized" = money collected on the stay.
The claim was paid/satisfied; the property won't be sold.
Service of the writ/notice on the defendant has been made.
Pa.R.C.P. 3129.2 — notice of sale (handbills, written notice to owners/lienholders, publication). Written notice must be served at least 30 days before the sale; the Sheriff rejects late ones.

Pa.R.C.P. 3129.3 — postponement of sale / new notice. Needed when a sale was postponed to this date. Often filed in the last day or two before the sale, which is why cases missing only this item are listed on Almost Ready.
Sheriff has everything needed and has cleared the property to sell on this date.
Order of court. "NEED O/C FOR [dates]" = a court order approving the chain of postponements through those sale dates; the Sheriff rejects orders that skip a date or list them out of sequence.
Bankruptcy / bankruptcy dismissal or relief-from-stay docs. A pending bankruptcy automatically stays the sale until the Sheriff receives the dismissal or relief order.
No service made on the defendant(s) — proof of service still needed.
Save Your Home — Allegheny County foreclosure-diversion/conciliation program.
Plaintiff owes the Sheriff an additional cost deposit; the case cannot go to sale until paid.
Court order updating the judgment amount (the most recent figure is shown in the sheet).
A previous winning bidder failed to pay the balance and lost the deposit; the property is being re-offered.
Sale advertising materials. If late or incorrect, the Sheriff requires a postponement.

Whether a federal tax lien is discharged depends on whether the United States was properly joined. When it is joined, the IRS generally keeps a right to redeem (buy back) the property after the sale (28 U.S.C. § 2410(c); IRM 5.12.5).
PA planned-community and condo statutes give associations limited priority (about six months of assessments) over a first mortgage; the rest of the HOA debt is junior.
Commonwealth Dept. of Human Services lien (e.g., estate recovery). Check whether it is divested.
Land bank involvement noted on the case — confirm whether a land bank intends to bid or has priority before investing time.

OK to Sell = Active, residential, Sheriff OK box checked, and no outstanding items in the notes other than Rule 3129.3. Almost Ready = Active, residential, Service and 3129.2 boxes checked, and the only outstanding item is Rule 3129.3 — plus "VERIFY" cases where the OK box and the notes disagree. Everything else (postponed, stayed, paid, bankruptcy, court orders or service still needed, commercial / industrial / vacant land) is left off the sheet.

Allegheny County Sheriff — Sale Listings PDF from sheriffalleghenycounty.com/sheriffs-sales/. The Sheriff states the binding bid list is finalized the morning of the sale; the version and print time used for the latest update are on the Overview tab.
Realty transfer tax on a sheriff deed

1% state + 1%–4% local depending on municipality and school district (2% in most suburbs, 5% in the City of Pittsburgh). On sheriff, foreclosure and tax-sale deeds the base is computed value (assessed value × CLR factor, 2.03 for 7/1/2026–6/30/2027), not the bid (61 Pa. Code § 91.135). With no seller to split it, the buyer bears it. See the Transfer Tax sheet.
